intro: Paphos drivers face narrow old town lanes, busy coastal roundabouts, and fast highway links, so picking the right driving school matters more here than in most Cyprus cities.

schools.8905662a5551383e: Costas Constantinou Driving School sits on Konstantinou Kanari street in central Paphos, postcode 8010, putting learners close to Kato Paphos, the harbour road, and the Tombs of the Kings area. The school holds a perfect 5.0 rating from 15 reviews, the strongest review count of any top-rated school in the city. Students often mention calm instruction and clear feedback after each lesson. The central base means you practise real Paphos traffic from the first hour: tight one-way streets near the old market, school-zone slow points, and the busy Apostolou Pavlou avenue that links the upper town with the seafront. Lessons usually cover roundabout discipline, hill starts on the streets climbing toward Mesogi, and parallel parking in tight residential blocks. For learners who want steady coaching and a strong track record close to the town centre, this is a solid first call.
schools.4c5d29575db5f20f: Scholi Odigon Savvas Giota is based at Nikou Antoniadi 10, in the 8046 district of Paphos, a quiet residential pocket near the Anavargos side of the city. The school carries a 5.0 rating, and although review numbers are smaller, feedback points to patient, family-style teaching. The location is useful for learners who live in the western suburbs or study at nearby colleges, since lessons can begin in calmer streets before moving onto the heavier traffic of Eleftheriou Venizelou and the route down to the coastal strip. Instructors here typically build confidence in stages: slow-speed control, mirror and signal habits, then highway merging toward the A6 Limassol road. The mix of quiet starts and gradual exposure to real Paphos conditions suits nervous beginners and anyone returning to driving after a long break.
schools.a3e0f1b78dc791c5: Scholi Odigon Fikardos operates from Leoforos Mesogis in postcode 8280, on the road that climbs north out of Paphos toward Mesogi and Tsada. The 5.0 rating reflects strong learner satisfaction. The Mesogi road is one of the most useful training routes in the city: it has steady uphill gradients, blind bends, village junctions, and a steady flow of tourist traffic during summer. Learners with Fikardos get used to gear control on slopes, safe overtaking on rural stretches, and reading the road surface, which can change quickly after rain. The school is also well placed for residents of Mesogi, Marathounta, and Konia who want lessons close to home. Expect a practical, road-focused style with attention to the kind of mixed urban and semi-rural driving that defines daily life in greater Paphos.
schools.417efc336c6ea131: Delta School of Motoring is also based on Leoforos Mesogis in the 8280 area, sharing the busy northern corridor of the city. It holds a 3.8 rating from 16 reviews, which gives it the largest feedback base in this group alongside a more mixed picture. Some learners praise the structured lesson plan and clear theory support, while others suggest asking about instructor availability before booking a block of lessons. The Mesogi base gives easy access to varied training ground: the climb up to Tsada for hill work, the descent into central Paphos for urban practice, and the link roads toward Geroskipou and the A6 highway for higher-speed driving. Delta can suit learners who want a school with a long local presence and a wide range of lesson slots across the week.

closing: Driving in Paphos has its own character, and good lessons should reflect that. The city splits roughly into Ktima, the upper town around the market, courts, and main bus station, and Kato Paphos, the lower coastal zone with the harbour, hotels, and archaeological park. Between them runs Apostolou Pavlou avenue, a long descending road with several roundabouts that catches out many new drivers. Learning to read these roundabouts, especially the one near the Kings Avenue Mall and the one at the bottom near the harbour, is a core Paphos skill. Traffic patterns change with the seasons. From June to September, tourist hire cars fill the coastal roads, and pedestrians cross suddenly near Coral Bay and the Tombs of the Kings strip. In winter, rain on worn asphalt around Mesogi, Tala, and the Chloraka bypass can make stopping distances longer than learners expect. The A6 highway toward Limassol is the main route for motorway practice, and instructors usually take students on it once basic control is solid. Junctions at Geroskipou, Timi, and the airport turnoff are the most common motorway exercises. Neighbourhoods such as Anavargos, Konia, Mesa Chorio, and Universal each have their own quirks: narrow lanes, parked cars on both sides, and steep side streets that test clutch control in manual cars. For the practical test, examiners in Paphos pay close attention to mirror checks, correct lane choice on multi-lane roundabouts, and smooth hill starts. Many test routes pass through residential zones with 30 km/h limits and school crossings, so speed discipline matters as much as parking accuracy. Theory test centres are based in the district offices in central Paphos, and most schools include theory support in their packages. Choosing a school close to where you live or work makes lesson scheduling easier, but it is also worth asking which test routes the instructor uses for mock drives. A school that prepares you on the exact streets used by examiners gives a real advantage. Paphos rewards drivers who stay calm, plan ahead, and respect the mix of locals, tourists, and delivery traffic that shares its roads every day.

faq.q: What is the minimum age to start driving lessons in Paphos?
faq.a: You can apply for a learner permit at 17 and a half and take the practical test from 18. Most Paphos schools accept bookings a few weeks before your 17 and a half birthday so lessons start on time.

faq.q: How many lessons do most learners need in Paphos?
faq.a: Most beginners take between 20 and 30 hours of lessons before the test. Learners who already drive abroad may need fewer, while those starting from zero on a manual car often need more practice on hill starts around Mesogi and Konia.

faq.q: Where is the driving test held in Paphos?
faq.a: The practical test is run by the Road Transport Department, with routes starting from the district office area in central Paphos. Routes usually cover Ktima streets, nearby residential zones, and at least one large roundabout.

faq.q: Can I learn on an automatic car in Paphos?
faq.a: Yes, several Paphos schools offer automatic lessons. Keep in mind that if you pass on an automatic, your licence will be limited to automatic cars only. For full flexibility, learn on a manual.

faq.q: How much do driving lessons cost in Paphos in 2026?
faq.a: Single lessons in Paphos generally range from about 25 to 35 euro per hour in 2026, with package deals lowering the per-lesson price. Test fees and learner permit costs are paid separately to the Road Transport Department.
